Therefore the place was named Abel Mizraim.' Correct answer: 'Abel Mizraim.' (1) 'Mahanaim' is the place where angels met Jacob, 32:2 (near_passage). (2) 'Bethel' is the place of the ladder, 28:19 (near_passage). (3) 'Galeed' is the heap of stones from the covenant with Laban, 31:48 (near_passage).

content: Just as Joseph had interpreted their dreams, what was the fate of the cupbearer and the baker?
options: Both officials were ultimately restored to their former positions by Pharaoh
Both officials were ultimately hanged by Pharaoh
The baker was released, while the cupbearer was put to death
The cupbearer was restored to his position, while the baker was hanged
explanation: Genesis 40:21-22 (ESV): 'He restored the chief cupbearer to his position... But he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.' Correct answer: 'The cupbearer was restored to his position, while the baker was hanged.' (1) 'Both were restored to their positions' is wrong: only one was (wrong_detail). (2) 'Both were hanged' is wrong (wrong_detail). (3) 'The fates of the two are reversed' gets the key detail wrong (wrong_detail).

content: When Joseph brought his father to meet Pharaoh, what notable thing did Jacob do?
options: Prostrated himself and presented many gifts to Pharaoh
Asked Pharaoh to grant him a title or rank
Blessed Pharaoh (the greater blessing the lesser)
Firmly refused to appear before Pharaoh
explanation: Genesis 47:7-10 (ESV): 'Then Joseph brought in Jacob his father and stood him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh'—both when he entered and when he departed. By custom, the greater blesses the lesser (cf. Hebrews 7:7). Correct answer: 'Blessed Pharaoh.' (1) 'Prostrated himself and presented gifts' is not in the text at this point (wrong_detail). (2) 'Asked for a title' is contrary to Jacob's standing as patriarch (wrong_detail). (3) 'Refused to appear' contradicts the text: he came and stood before Pharaoh (wrong_detail).

content: What occupation did Joseph instruct his brothers to tell Pharaoh they practiced, so they could settle in the land of Goshen?
options: That they were high-ranking officials in the Egyptian court
That they were keepers of livestock, since shepherds were detestable to Egyptians
That they were traveling merchants trading in distant lands
That they were priests serving God
explanation: Genesis 46:33-34 (ESV): Joseph instructed them: 'When Pharaoh calls you and says, "What is your occupation?" you shall say, "Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now," in order that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.' Correct answer: 'That they were keepers of livestock.' (1) 'High-ranking officials in the Egyptian court' is a fabricated detail (wrong_detail). (2) 'Traveling merchants in distant lands' is a fabricated detail (wrong_detail). (3) 'Priests serving God' is a fabricated detail (wrong_detail).

content: After their father died, Joseph's brothers feared he would take revenge on them; with what spirit did he respond?
options: He required all of them to serve as his slaves for life to atone for their past sins
He immediately drove all his brothers out of the land of Egypt
He remained completely silent, said nothing to them, and kept his distance from them
He reassured them, saying 'Am I in the place of God?', then promised to provide for them
explanation: Genesis 50:19-21 (ESV): Joseph said, 'Do not fear, for am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good... So do not fear; I will provide for you and your little ones.' The correct answer: 'He reassured them — Am I in the place of God? — and promised to provide for them.' (1) 'Requiring them to be slaves to atone for sin' contradicts his spirit of forgiveness (wrong_detail). (2) 'Driving them out of Egypt' is the opposite: he promised to provide for them (wrong_detail). (3) 'Remaining silent and keeping his distance' contradicts the text: he comforted them and spoke kindly to them (wrong_detail).

content: To test his brothers, what did Joseph instruct to be hidden in Benjamin's sack before sending men to pursue them?
options: A pouch filled with pure gold taken from the royal treasury
A small idol cast from pure silver
His silver cup, which was said to be used for divination
His signet ring together with the prime minister's finest robe
explanation: Genesis 44:2,5 (ESV): Joseph instructed his steward, 'Put my silver cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest'; then he sent men after them who said, 'Is it not from this that my lord drinks, and by this that he practices divination?' The correct answer: 'His silver cup, said to be used for divination.' (1) 'A pouch of gold from the royal treasury' is a fabricated detail (wrong_detail). (2) 'A silver idol' confuses this with the household gods Rachel stole from Laban, 31:19 (near_passage). (3) 'The signet ring and prime minister's robe' were what Pharaoh gave Joseph, 41:42 — not the item hidden in the sack (near_passage).

content: During the years of famine, what major consequence did Joseph's policy bring about for all of Egypt?
options: The people throughout the land revolted and overthrew Pharaoh's throne
All the land and the people became Pharaoh's possession, required to give a fifth of their produce
All the Egyptians were forced to relocate and live in the land of Canaan
Pharaoh was compelled to divide all the land equally among the people
explanation: Genesis 47:20-26 (ESV): Because of the famine, the Egyptians sold their livestock, then their land and themselves to buy grain; 'Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh,' and he established a statute that the people give a fifth of their harvest to Pharaoh. The correct answer: 'All the land and the people became Pharaoh's possession, required to give a fifth.' (1) 'The people revolted and overthrew Pharaoh' contradicts the text: the people were grateful for being kept alive (wrong_detail). (2) 'Relocating to Canaan' is a fabricated detail (wrong_detail). (3) 'Dividing the land equally among the people' is the exact opposite: the land was consolidated under Pharaoh (wrong_detail).
